reforms.description: The United States increased federal budget outlays for research as part of a broader fiscal expansion. The text explicitly mentions 'research' among the priority areas for increased federal spending in 1961.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Increased public R&D funding expands the knowledge base and research capacity, supporting long-term productivity growth and innovation.
reforms.status_evidence: The text states 'The emphasis of fiscal policy has been on higher expenditures' and lists 'research' among the areas covered by increased budget outlays.
reforms.importance_rationale: While research funding was increased as part of broader fiscal stimulus, the text provides no detail on the magnitude, scope, or structural nature of the change. It appears to be an incremental adjustment within a general expansion rather than a system-wide reform.
reforms.source_quote: The emphasis of fiscal policy has been on higher expenditures. The increase in budget outlays covers a wide range including defence, space programmes, education and research, foreign aid, housing and community development.
